display.name: vLLM
display.description: vLLM inference server health from the native vllm:* metrics. Covers token throughput, time to first token, inter-token and end-to-end latency, queue time, running and waiting requests, KV cache usage, prefix cache hit rate, and preemptions.

display.name: model_name
display.description: Filter panels to one model served by this vLLM server.

display.name: Output Token Throughput (tokens/s)
display.description: Headline decode throughput: the per-second rate of vllm:generation_tokens_total. vLLM ships no ready-made throughput gauge, so this is a rate over the cumulative counter.

display.name: Prompt vs Generation Token Rate (tokens/s)
display.description: Prefill (prompt) against decode (generation) token rate. A prompt-heavy shape points at long inputs and prefill-bound work; a generation-heavy shape points at long outputs and decode-bound work.

display.name: Time to First Token (p50 / p95 / p99)
display.description: How long a caller waits before the first token arrives. Read from vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds.bucket, the series the Collector splits the Prometheus histogram into. Rising TTFT with a flat token rate usually means requests are queueing rather than decoding slowly.

display.name: Inter-Token Latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
display.description: Gap between consecutive output tokens once decoding has started, from vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds.bucket. This is what a user perceives as streaming speed.

display.name: End-to-End Request Latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
display.description: Total wall-clock time per request, from vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds.bucket. It covers queue time, prefill and the whole decode, so it tracks output length as much as server health.

display.name: Request Queue Time (p50 / p95 / p99)
display.description: Time a request spends in the WAITING phase before the scheduler admits it, from vllm:request_queue_time_seconds.bucket. Queue time is the part of TTFT you fix with capacity, not with a faster model.

display.name: Running vs Waiting Requests
display.description: Requests the scheduler currently has in a model execution batch against requests still waiting for a slot. A waiting count that stays above zero means the server is saturated at its current max_num_seqs or KV cache budget.

display.name: KV Cache Usage
display.description: Fraction of the KV cache block pool in use, from the vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc gauge (vLLM reports 0-1, not 0-100). Sustained readings near 1 are what push the scheduler into preemption.

display.name: Prefix Cache Hit Rate
display.description: Share of queried prefix tokens served from the prefix cache. vLLM exposes no hit-rate metric, so this is a formula over the two counters: rate(vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total) / rate(vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total). A high hit rate is what keeps prefill cheap on repeated system prompts.

display.name: Preemption Rate
display.description: Requests per second the engine preempted and will have to recompute, from vllm:num_preemptions_total. Any sustained non-zero value means the KV cache is oversubscribed; it is the usual explanation for a latency spike that the token rate alone does not account for.
